reference_role: Only accepted Enemy 1021 identity, equipment, drawing scale, camera, boot/root anchor and green background. No Enemy 1011 pose image or HitRight pose uploaded.
prompt:
Edit the supplied green-screen Idle image of Enemy 1021 into one peak pose for the generic HitFlash damage reaction. This is a single 2D game-sprite pose on a fixed canvas, not a video, storyboard or environmental illustration. The supplied image is the sole identity authority. Preserve the same soldier, helmet, faceplate, red plume, armor, wooden shield, leather, belt, boots, proportions, pixel density, palette and lighting.

CAUSE: One light-to-medium invisible off-screen impact directly strikes the upper chest, causing a brief passive bodily flinch. This damage was NOT blocked by the shield. Express the injury through front-readable joint articulation only. Do not show shield-face impact absorption, intentional blocking or an intentional attack.

PRIMARY READ - SYMMETRIC CHEST/SHOULDER COMPRESSION AND A SHORTENED NECK: Both shoulder plates jerk upward and inward. The neck compresses and the helmet settles slightly downward toward the collar, visibly nestled between the raised shoulder plates. The chest tightens with a local contraction between upper chest and abdomen. Do not substitute whole-character scaling, inflation or flattening for joint movement. Keep the helmet and faceplate facing the camera, with the head on the chest centerline. No head tilt to either side, side turn or bowed ducking pose. A brief narrowing of the eye slit is allowed, but do not redesign the eyes or faceplate. The compressed neck-and-shoulder relationship must be visibly different from Idle.

SHIELD AND ARMS: Keep the same wooden shield in its original hand on SCREEN-LEFT. The hit relaxes the shield elbow slightly, letting the shield settle passively a little down and toward SCREEN-LEFT with only a small outward angle. Its inner edge moves away from part of the chest armor, leaving a clearly readable narrow exposed chest area rather than completely covering the front of the body. Keep this compact: do not spread the shield arm far sideways or make a wide-open off-side recoil pose. Preserve the original grip connection; no hand swap, side switch, release, break or disappearance. The empty SCREEN-RIGHT arm has a short reflexive elbow bend with the wrist trailing slightly downward. It does not deliberately guard the chest, clutch the head or make a boxing pose.

Both knees absorb the force with slight flexion, while the belt and pelvis remain near their original positions and both boots keep the reference contact points. Root position stays fixed. No step, slide, becoming airborne, kneeling, deep squat or fall. Any apparent shortening must come from neck/shoulder and joint relationships; drawing scale and the physical size of each body part stay unchanged. The red plume and cloth have only a small passive inertial response, without a new exaggerated arc.

Preserve the 1024x1024 canvas, locked orthographic front-facing camera and original framing. Keep the full helmet, shield, arms, legs, boots and red plume inside the canvas with at least 15% empty safety margin on every side. No recentering, cropping, zooming out or rescaling. Keep the cool iron-gray and blue-gray armor, sharp silver highlights, crimson cloth, warm brown leather and wooden shield, dark iron fittings, crisp stepped pixel contours and clustered value shapes. Do not convert to smooth illustration or add random pixel noise.

Keep a flat opaque chroma-green background RGB(0,177,64). No light-gray or white plate, checkerboard, gradient, floor, cast shadow or green environmental lighting. Green belongs only to the background; do not tint the armor, cloth, shield or outlines green.

DO NOT include an attacker, entering weapon, sparks, flashes, blood, dust, smoke, debris, speed lines, shockwaves, afterimages or any other effect; an intentional shield raise, block or shield bash, shield-face impact absorption, a shield fully covering the chest, a wide sideways shield opening, swapped hand or dropped shield; head tilt to either side, body lean, whole-body twist, three-quarter view, profile or mirrored image; stepping, sliding, hopping, launching, kneeling, deep squat or falling; whole-character translation, scaling, inflation, squash, stretch or camera movement; changed helmet, faceplate, armor plates, shield shape, limb count, palette or materials; gray or white background, transparency, checkerboard, background gradient, scenery, text, UI, watermark or extra character.
